An empty missing-evidence list can mean the check was skipped.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for quality checks
sections.what: Brings in the industry structure and a helper that says whether an industry accepts any label.
sections.why: Lets the checks compare project data with the official industry tree.

sections.name: collectNodeNames, LEAF_CACHE
sections.title: Gathers allowed category names
sections.what: Walks an industry's tree and collects every name at every level, then remembers the result so it is not rebuilt each time.
sections.why: The comments say this matches how classification is done elsewhere, so both agree.
sections.watch_out: Any name anywhere in the tree counts as allowed, so a label placed at the wrong level still passes.

sections.name: taxonomyLeaves, QAProject, FieldCompleteness, DriftRow, QualityReport, CORE_FIELDS
sections.title: Shapes and core fields for quality data
sections.what: Defines the shapes for a project summary, a completeness row, a drift row and the full report. Lists the seven core fields checked, and includes a helper that treats blank, null or NaN as empty.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond defining the report structure.
sections.watch_out: The core field list is the only place that decides which fields count, so editing it changes every completeness figure.

sections.name: fieldCompleteness
sections.title: Share of projects with each field
sections.what: For each core field, counts the projects that have a value and returns that count with a rounded percentage.
sections.why: Shows where the data is thin.
sections.watch_out: Zero counts as filled, so a real zero that means nothing can look complete.

sections.name: taxonomyDrift
sections.title: Finds bad or missing sub-industries
sections.what: Flags projects with no sub-industry as missing. In strict industries it also flags any sub-industry that is not on the allowed list. Data-driven industries accept any value.
sections.why: Keeps categories consistent in industries that have a fixed list.
sections.watch_out: Projects in data-driven industries are never flagged for unknown labels, so their categories can drift without notice.

sections.name: buildQualityReport
sections.title: Assembles the full quality report
sections.what: Combines the timestamp, project total, industry counts, completeness, drift, missing evidence and low-confidence lists into one report. The confidence threshold defaults to 40.
sections.why: Gives callers a single function that returns the whole report.
sections.watch_out: Missing evidence is empty unless evidence counts are passed in, so an empty list does not prove every project has evidence.

summary: Calculates quality checks for project data: how complete the core fields are, which projects have unrecognized sub-industry labels, and which lack evidence or have low confidence.
purpose: Produces a quality report that shows gaps in the project database.
why: Likely reason: to keep the data trustworthy. Not otherwise stated.
how: 1. Collects every allowed sub-industry name for each industry and caches the list. 2. Counts how many projects fill each core field. 3. Flags projects with no sub-industry, and in strict industries flags any sub-industry not on the allowed list. 4. Counts projects with no evidence, if evidence counts are given. 5. Flags projects with confidence below 40 by default. 6. Bundles the results with a timestamp and per-industry counts.
inputs: A list of project summaries, optional evidence counts per project, and an optional confidence threshold.
outputs: A report with totals by industry, completeness percentages, taxonomy drift rows, missing-evidence rows and low-confidence rows.
risks: A project with no confidence score counts as zero and is flagged as low confidence. Missing-evidence results appear only when evidence counts are supplied, so an empty list can look like a clean result when nothing was checked.
debug: If the report looks wrong, compare the project's sub-industry with its industry structure. Check the default confidence threshold of 40. If missing evidence is always empty, confirm that evidence counts are passed in.
